title: GPT-5.6 segment and product temporal drift recheck
question: Which GPT-5.6 facts changed or remained temporally split across source segments and product surfaces, and what can a repeat capture honestly supersede?

inclusion_criteria: Use bounded source segments and retain product, runtime, instrument, and temporal identity.
Prefer official facts, exposed independent methods, primary traces, and explicit counterevidence.
Preserve incomplete operational evidence only in the role and scope it can support.
exclusion_criteria: Do not count dependent retellings as independent origins.
Do not infer model-only traits from product, runtime, transport, quota, or harness symptoms.
Do not compare aggregate scores across instrument revisions as a longitudinal model result.

generality_probe.rationale: The run tests whether one family label survives separate product and instrument timelines without schema changes.

clusters.label: Currentness is segment-local rather than URL-wide
clusters.supported_scope: Within the captured OpenAI provider surfaces, prices and benchmark values require dated segment identity because one live URL can retain historical prose beside later corrections.
transfer_limits: One provider origin establishes the document behavior but not cross-publisher prevalence.
unresolved_configuration_gaps: Exact source-byte archives and provider edit history are unavailable.
clusters.next_action: Retain segment locators/digests and create new observations on future changes instead of mutating history.

clusters.label: Family-tier identity requires product and release-time binding
clusters.supported_scope: For the August 2026 OpenAI product split, the Sol or Luna tier label alone cannot identify the Chat model versus the prior Work/Codex model.
transfer_limits: Does not establish exact snapshots or behavioral deltas between products.
clusters.next_action: Require product and temporal binding in any future realization candidate.

clusters.label: API capacity and Codex realization require separate route identity
clusters.supported_scope: Across provider and two independent primary traces, the family label under-identifies API capacity, product-time subject, catalog ceiling and local-tool route realization.
transfer_limits: The two issue mechanisms differ and neither is an owner runtime diagnosis.
unresolved_configuration_gaps: Exact snapshots, backend entitlement cause and owner runtime subjects remain absent.
clusters.next_action: Replicate exact route fields against an owner-bound runtime subject before changing any realization.

clusters.label: Quota interruption belongs to product termination economics
clusters.supported_scope: One bounded goal shows that a product usage boundary can terminate and require recovery independently of whether the model could continue the task.
transfer_limits: No population incidence, token accounting or accepted artifact is available.
unresolved_configuration_gaps: Exact plan ledger, task state at interruption and recovery outcome are unknown.
clusters.next_action: Measure interruption, checkpoint, resume and accepted-outcome denominators on owned long goals.

tensions.label: Retained launch prices versus current API prices
tensions.analysis: The values are not competing current facts: one segment preserves launch history while current model pages and dated notices establish later effective prices.
tensions.remaining_question: When will the temporary Sol reduction expire or be replaced by another current price?

tensions.label: Shared tier label versus distinct product-time realization
tensions.analysis: The provider itself distinguishes the subjects despite shared family labels and risk designations, so label equality cannot collapse product-time identity.
tensions.remaining_question: Will future product surfaces converge on one exposed snapshot or continue independent cadence?

tensions.label: Documented API context versus realized Codex catalog ceiling
tensions.analysis: The values belong to different product and route authority layers; the issue does not revise the API specification and the API page does not guarantee a Codex session ceiling.
tensions.remaining_question: Which exact backend policy maps account, originator and client build to the effective ceiling?

tensions.label: Long-horizon capability versus product-window interruption
tensions.analysis: A model/product may support long work while a separate usage policy terminates one execution; capability and recoverable completion remain different axes.
tensions.remaining_question: What fraction of owned long goals checkpoint, resume and reach accepted completion across product limits?

method_pressures.pressure: Mutable pages can contain simultaneously current, historical, and corrected segments.
method_pressures.proposed_response: Bind currentness, digests, and supersession to source segments rather than URLs.

method_pressures.pressure: Family and tier labels under-identify models when products advance on separate cadences.
method_pressures.proposed_response: Require product and effective interval before any realization or behavior review.

method_pressures.pressure: A corrected metric label can materially change a benchmark value without changing its URL.
method_pressures.proposed_response: Preserve old and corrected observations with the metric denominator and change date.

method_pressures.pressure: Repeated provider documentation can look like corroboration while remaining one evidence origin.
method_pressures.proposed_response: Track dependency refs and do not increment origin independence for restatements.

method_pressures.pressure: A current family label and model specification can coexist with route-specific catalog and tool-host realizations.
method_pressures.proposed_response: Bind capacity and tool observations to product, originator/client route, runtime build and exact owner subject when available.

method_pressures.pressure: Quota complaints become useful only when interruption, goal state, resume path and accepted outcome have denominators.
method_pressures.proposed_response: Keep product quota in the outcome termination and recovery ledger instead of converting it into model efficiency.

revisit_triggers: OpenAI changes any GPT-5.6 base or long-context price.
Chat, Work, Codex, or API exposes a new snapshot or converges on one version.
The safety card or benchmark change log receives another correction.
The temporary Sol price reduction reaches its stated three-month horizon.
The cited Codex catalog or code-mode issues receive provider confirmation, a fix, closure, or an independent controlled reproduction.
Codex publishes an exact accounting and checkpoint/resume contract for short-window quota interruptions.
